description: This program elective develops an understanding of the concept of optimization and its theory. Students analyse the advantages and disadvantages of large-scale optimization techniques applied to engineering problems and implement selected optimization algorithms for engineering systems.

syllabus.title: Introduction and Convex Analysis
syllabus.body: Introduction to optimization theory, its importance in solving system engineering problems, convex sets and functions, supporting and separating hyperplanes, dual cones and generalized inequalities, multi-objective optimization.

syllabus.title: Linear and Dynamic Programming
syllabus.body: Linear programming problem: formulation and solution by different methods, duality in linear programming, sensitivity analysis, integer linear programming, linear programming approach to game theory, dynamic programming problems.

syllabus.title: Nonlinear Programming
syllabus.body: Introduction to nonlinear programming: unconstrained optimization and formulation of quadratic optimization problems; constrained optimization, quadratic programming, separable programming.

syllabus.title: Heuristic Optimization and Applications
syllabus.body: Brief introduction to heuristic optimization, convex and non-convex optimization, application of optimization in different fields, case study and simulation.

outcomes: Understand the different optimization algorithms and multidisciplinary design optimization, and formulate optimization problems.
Apply knowledge of optimization to formulate and solve engineering problems.
Understand the different methods of optimization and suggest a technique for a specific problem.
textbooks: S. S. Rao, Optimization Theory and Applications, Wiley Eastern Ltd.
S. Boyd and L. Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, Cambridge University Press.
Hamdy A. Taha, Operations Research: An Introduction, Pearson Prentice Hall.
referenceBooks: D. Bertsekas, Nonlinear Programming, Athena Scientific.
V. Chvatal, Linear Programming, W. H. Freeman, New York.
R. Fletcher, Practical Methods of Optimization, Wiley, New York.
